evidence: Exhaustive grep for 'ghost' across src/stats.ts, src/insights.tsx, src/format.ts, worker/index.ts finds no rate/ratio computation anywhere. What exists: 'ghosted' is one of three TERMINAL_STATUSES (src/types.ts:13), used only for status classification (isDead in src/format.ts:106) and to EXCLUDE apps from funnel/response-rate math (src/stats.ts funnelReachCounts/funnelConversions/responseRate all key off FUNNEL_STAGES, which does not include ghosted; worker/index.ts:1420,2008,2039 filter '!= ghosted' for open/live counts). The only ghosting-adjacent figure is a raw COUNT inside outcomeBreakdown (src/stats.ts:241-272): ghosted apps' outcome_reason ('no_reply_after_applying'/'went_quiet_mid_process'/'other') tallied as bar counts, never divided by any denominator (total applications, total applied, etc.) anywhere in the codebase. PRODUCT.md:19,27,43 and README.md:23 all name 'ghost rate' as a shipped diagnostic; no such rate exists in code.

worker/index.ts:1991-1994 computes recentMoves/priorMoves then at 2030-2035 derives momentum with NO minimum-event floor: 'if (recentMoves===0 && priorMoves===0) quiet; else if (priorMoves===0) faster; else change=(recentMoves-priorMoves)/priorMoves...'. src/format.ts:470-505 (computePipelineMomentum) has MOMENTUM_MIN_EVENTS=6 and an explicit 'early' verdict when recent+prior<6, with a comment describing exactly this scenario as the bug being fixed ('the old code called prior===0 with any recent movement speeding up... at full confidence'). Divergent input: recentMoves=1, priorMoves=0 (1 total event). In-app (format.ts): recent+prior=1<6 -> verdict='early' (no confident claim shown). Public share page (worker/index.ts): priorMoves===0 branch fires -> momentum=S.faster, i.e. the page prints 'Speeding up' off a single stage advance -- the exact overconfident behavior format.ts's own comment says was fixed. The share page never imports/uses MOMENTUM_MIN_EVENTS or computePipelineMomentum; it reimplements the pre-fix logic inline.

src/stats.ts:91-104 documents that medianTimeInStageDays (the only prior generalized time-in-stage function) was deliberately DELETED for mixing censored/complete durations; it is not present anywhere in stats.ts:1-280 today. The only duration-like metric implemented is responseTime (src/stats.ts:178-224), and it covers exactly one stage boundary: 'applied' -> first subsequent transition (the reply). No equivalent exists for screening/interview/offer dwell time; medianTimeToOffer (src/format.ts:529-565) is a different metric (applied->offer span, not per-stage dwell). Second question (censoring): responseTime EXCLUDES still-open apps from the median -- 'answered' (rows with a next transition) feed the median (stats.ts:213); 'waits' (no next transition, i.e. censored/still-in-stage) are collected separately and reported only as waiting/longestWait/beyondAnyReply, never mixed into the median array. This is deliberate and extensively documented (stats.ts:161-177): including censored rows would bias the median down ('a fresh batch of ten applications sent yesterday would report a median response of one day'); excluding them is the chosen tradeoff, acknowledged in-code as still imperfect but preferable ('the pair of numbers... is the honest reading'). So: excluded, not included -- the safer of the two biases, and already reasoned about in the comments rather than a hidden defect.

worker/demo.ts:227-238 inserts an application with status='ghosted' and then writes exactly ONE status_history row: (NULL, 'ghosted') (line 235). src/stats.ts reachedIndexByApp only records an app if some row's to_status is in FUNNEL_STAGES=[interested,applied,screening,interview,offer]; 'ghosted' is not in that list, so this app is never added to the reached map at all and is invisible to funnelReachCounts/funnelConversions/responseRate at every index, including i=0 ('reached interested') -- despite being a real seeded application. It IS visible in outcomeBreakdown (counted as an unrecorded closed outcome) and on the board (applications.status). HOWEVER: the live seeded DB at .wrangler/state/v3/d1/.../*.sqlite was NOT populated by worker/demo.ts's seedSampleData -- it matches scripts/seed-demo.sql (different fictional company names entirely: 'Northwind Cloud', 'Lumen Robotics', etc., none of which appear in worker/demo.ts). That fixture gives every one of its 18 applications a proper NULL->interested genesis row first (verified: 'SELECT... where first_to not in funnel stages' returns 0 rows; 0 apps with zero history rows). So the bug is real and reproducible by reading worker/demo.ts, but not demonstrable from this particular live DB snapshot, which happens to use a hand-written fixture that already avoids the pattern.

worker/public-api.ts api.post('/applications') (~381-421, mounted at /api/v1 via app.route, line 436) inserts into applications with status='interested' and writes NO status_history row, unlike worker/index.ts:754 (session create path) and worker/feed.ts:625-629 (feed-add path), both of which insert a (NULL, status) genesis row. Blast radius by consumer (grep status_history across worker/ and src/): (1) src/stats.ts funnelReachCounts/funnelConversions/responseRate (reachedIndexByApp) -- an extension-created app that never advances past 'interested' has ZERO status_history rows and is fully invisible at every funnel index, including the base 'reached interested' count; the applications table clearly shows it exists, but every history-derived metric acts as if it doesn't. (2) worker/index.ts:1479-1535 (/api/stats) and :1955-1965 (public /shared/:token page) both read status_history the same way, so the app is equally invisible on the public share page's funnel. (3) worker/digest.ts 'advanced' count (status_history rows this week with rank(to)>rank(from)) never fires for such an app's creation week (no genesis row to rank), unlike normally-created apps, so weekly-digest 'advanced' undercounts extension adds; 'added' (off applications.created_at) is unaffected. (4) outcomeBreakdown is unaffected unless/until the app reaches a terminal status, at which point it behaves normally. Self-heal check: recordStatusChange (worker/index.ts:199-218) takes `from` as an explicit parameter; its two call sites (lines 893, 925) pass `existing.status` -- read directly from the applications table row, NOT derived from status_history. So the FIRST real status change after extension-create writes a correct, non-NULL from_status (e.g. 'interested'->'applied') without needing any prior history row -- the transition itself self-heals. But the genesis moment (to_status='interested') is permanently lost: reachedIndexByApp records only the app's max to_status ever seen, so once the app advances to 'applied' it does get retroactively counted at i=0 too (since reached-applied implies reached-interested in the r>=i filter) -- the permanent, unrecoverable gap is confined to apps that are created via the extension and NEVER advance past 'interested'; those remain invisible to every status_history-based metric forever. Could not pull live row counts: the seeded DB (scripts/seed-demo.sql fixture) contains zero source='extension' rows and zero applications with no status_history rows at all (checked directly), so this DB cannot empirically demonstrate the gap -- the finding rests on static code tracing, not observed data.

src/types.ts:29-42 (OUTCOME_REASONS) scopes reason vocabularies per terminal status: rejected=[no_response, after_screening, after_interview, role_cancelled, other], ghosted=[no_reply_after_applying, went_quiet_mid_process, other]. worker/index.ts:955-957 validates a submitted reason against the vocabulary for that row's own to_status specifically because mixing them 'would poison the breakdown' (e.g. comp_too_low doesn't apply to ghosted). outcomeBreakdown (src/stats.ts:241-272) renders one bar per distinct reason slug across all closed statuses (confirmed via src/insights.tsx:372-375, a flat outcomes.counts.map), so 'rejected/no_response' and 'ghosted/no_reply_after_applying' do render as two separate bars. But this reflects a real, pre-existing product distinction, not a computation bug: status='rejected' vs status='ghosted' is a deliberate choice the user already made when closing the application (rejected implies some rejection signal was received, even if generic/unexplained; ghosted implies literally nothing was ever said). outcomeBreakdown faithfully reports outcomes for whichever status the user picked; it does not itself conflate or double-count anything, and the per-status reason validation exists specifically to keep the two vocabularies from bleeding into each other. The one legitimate weakness is a copy/labeling ambiguity -- 'no_response' under 'rejected' and 'no_reply_after_applying' under 'ghosted' both render as similar English ('No response' vs 'No reply after applying'), which could read as the same underlying experience split arbitrarily -- but that is a wording nit in en.json/nl.json, not a defect in outcomeBreakdown's logic or a miscomputed number.
